name: Posttraumatic stress disorder
summary: Intrusion, avoidance, negative mood/cognition, and hyperarousal after trauma lasting more than 1 month. Only sertraline and paroxetine are FDA-labeled for PTSD. Trauma-focused psychotherapy is preferred over medication in VA/DoD 2023. FDA declined MDMA-assisted therapy (CRL, Aug 2024) and brexpiprazole plus sertraline (CRL, Sept 2025). Methylone (TSND-201) received a priority voucher in 2026 but has no approval.
plainSummary: PTSD can follow a frightening or dangerous event. It brings upsetting memories, nightmares, avoiding reminders, and feeling on edge. Trauma-focused therapy works best, and some antidepressants also help.

dosing.start: 25 mg once daily for 1 week, then 50 mg
dosing.notes: Increase by 25–50 mg/day once weekly. Mild hepatic impairment: half the usual dose; not recommended in moderate or severe impairment.

boxedWarnings: Suicidal thoughts and behaviors in children, adolescents, and young adults
contraindications: MAOIs (including linezolid or IV methylene blue) concurrently or within 14 days
approved.plainSummary: Sertraline is a daily antidepressant (SSRI) approved for PTSD in adults. It can ease intrusive memories, avoidance, and feeling on edge.

approved.plainSummary: Paroxetine is a daily antidepressant (SSRI) approved for PTSD in adults. Stopping it suddenly can cause withdrawal-like symptoms.

verified.note: Label reformatted Sept 2026; maximum for PTSD listed as 50 mg/day.

offLabel.notes: VA/DoD 2023 gives a strong recommendation for paroxetine, sertraline, or venlafaxine; the American Psychological Association 2017 guideline also conditionally recommends it. Not FDA-labeled for PTSD. Can raise blood pressure; discontinuation symptoms.

offLabel.notes: VA/DoD 2023 suggests prazosin for PTSD nightmares (weak for) but suggests against it for overall PTSD symptoms. A large VA trial (Raskind 2018) found no benefit over placebo; AASM 2018 lists it as 'may be used'. Titrate slowly from a low bedtime dose; cautions: orthostatic hypotension, first-dose syncope, dizziness.

offLabel.notes: Small, mixed RCTs; meta-analyses suggest at most a small effect on hyperarousal. VA/DoD 2023: insufficient evidence for or against. Cautions: cognitive slowing, paresthesias, kidney stones, metabolic acidosis, angle-closure glaucoma, teratogenicity.

offLabel.notes: Commonly used, but VA/DoD 2023 suggests against antipsychotic augmentation (weak against), including brexpiprazole. The FDA issued a Complete Response Letter (Sept 2025) for brexpiprazole plus sertraline for PTSD after a 1–10 advisory committee vote on efficacy. Cautions: weight gain, metabolic effects, sedation, EPS/tardive dyskinesia.
